purpose: Design demonstration: bring trade-imports-ins-frontend into the same shape as the two journey frontends (animals, plants) without extracting a shared package, and backport the chassis hardening ins already has. Lands on one branch across every repo it touches, behind draft PRs that are never merged.
direction: ins moves toward animals/plants. Where animals and plants differ from each other, plants is the tidier fork; prefer its shape and say so. Journey-only layers (model, bridge, engine, flow, analysis, sets, obligation-purity, the L3/L4 dependency-cruiser rules) are never ported to ins.
invariants: Public URL surface of ins does not change: /, /address-book, /address-book/add, /address-book/{id}, /address-book/{id}/edit, /address-book/{id}/delete, /auth/*, /signout, /health. Other services and the tests repo link to these.
Behaviour is preserved unless the stage brief says otherwise. A stage that changes behaviour names the change in its notes.
The unit suite, lint, format:check and the Playwright suite are green at the end of every stage, because every stage is a commit on a shared branch that CI checks.
No new shared package, no cross-repo imports. Duplication is deliberate; alignment is the goal.
Every user-facing string that a stage touches or creates lives in copy.en.js and copy.cy.js with identical structure, once stage s07 exists. Before s07, strings stay where they are.
Comments are removed aggressively; no migration or rename comments; git history and app/docs carry the rationale.
Names are explicit and say what a thing does. No metaphors.
Mock at the network boundary (nock) in ins tests; do not introduce module-boundary mocks where a network mock exists.
